page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). Memory configuration totals 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. No discrete GPU acceleration is present, but local ephemeral storage is provided via a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-threaded performance contrasted with low multi-threaded throughput, as expected from a 2-core, 4-thread envelope. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,643.0 and stress-ng single-core result of 1,948.38, place in the middle 50% tier, with single-threaded gzip compression showing strong throughput at 31.35 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics like Geekbench multi-core (3,707.0), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (26.0 GB/sec), and stress-ng multi-core (3,991.37) place in the bottom 25%. Synthetic testing yields average ratings across PassMark CPU (7,381.13), PassMark memory (2,264.9), and static web serving throughput (7.57 GB/sec), while large block memory bandwidths (36.24 GB/sec read, 25.93 GB/sec write) and Redis SET operations (5.66 million ops/sec) remain in the lower tier.

The primary tradeoff of the E4ds_v6 lies in its resource prioritization: it provides high RAM capacity and fast local NVMe storage relative to core count, but computational capacity is limited by the underlying 2-physical-core ceiling. The server is well suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extensive parallel compute, such as relational databases, in-memory caching tiers, mid-scale data extraction and transformation (ETL), and small-model CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyperthreading) powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. It is paired with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, and includes a 236 GB local NVMe SSD. It contains no GPUs. Single-thread processing performs in average tiers, highlighted by strong single-threaded gzip compression at 31.35 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,643.0. However, multi-core processing falls in the bottom 25% due to its 2-core boundary, with multi-core Geekbench reaching 3,707.0. Given its high RAM-to-core density and bundled local high-speed NVMe storage, the E4ds_v6 is well suited for database engines, cache stores, ETL data pipelines, and moderate web serving layers that require high memory allocations without heavy multi-threaded CPU demands.
